summary: Remote-controlled shell execution via hardcoded signaling relay and WebRTC data channel
details: @vanexalabs-ai/vanexa-agent ships a Node agent whose primary artifact is V8 bytecode (dist/bundle.jsc) with an inspectable JS fallback (dist/bundle.cjs). When started (e.g. `vanexa-agent start`), the bundle opens a WebSocket to a hardcoded signaling relay at vanexa-agent-relay.tubefood.workers.dev (and vanexa-agent-relay.workers.dev), negotiates an RTCPeerConnection + DataChannel with a remote peer, and dispatches received `tool_call` messages into handlers that invoke execSync/spawn on the installer's host. The remote party — anyone who controls the paired peer or the author-operated relay — can execute arbitrary shell commands on the machine running the agent, granting full-host RCE. The `vanexa-agent update` path additionally fetches and executes https://vanexa-installer.vercel.app/install.sh (install.ps on Windows), a mutable, unversioned, unpinned, unverified endpoint on a publisher-controlled Vercel deployment, so any compromise of that deployment silently propagates arbitrary code to every user who runs update. The shipped socket.json disables Socket.dev issue rules for aiMalware, obfuscatedCode, usesEval, nativeCode, shellAccess, filesystemAccess, networkAccess, bypassesEnvironment, and installScripts, reducing third-party visibility into what commands the remote peer can drive.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
